member.name: T:Gum.Bundle.FontReferenceCollector
member.summary: Single source of truth for "what fonts does this project need bitmap-rendered?". Consumed by both HeadlessFontGenerationService.CollectRequiredFonts (used by gumcli fonts and the WPF tool) and (used by gumcli pack).
member.remarks:
Decoupled from the ObjectFinder.Self singleton via a constructor-injected element resolver so callers that don't (or shouldn't) populate the singleton can still use the collector.
Known limitation: this collector does NOT yet resolve StyleCategoryState indirection (where a TextInstance's StyleCategoryState property points at a state in a Styles component whose Strong.* variables should be pulled in as the resolved font for the referencing TextInstance). That's a deeper runtime-resolution gap that affects both gumcli fonts and gumcli pack equally; tracking separately.
Known limitation: a conditional (ternary) VariableReferences row on the element itself or a direct instance has every branch pregenerated (see #4042), but a conditional reference reached only through a nested component instance's inner Text instances (CollectFontsFromNestedTextInstances) still resolves a single value via - only the currently-active branch is collected there.

member.name: F:Gum.Bundle.FontReferenceCollector.FontAffectingVariableNames
member.summary: Font-affecting properties whose VariableReferences row is branch-enumerated (all ternary branches collected, not just the one active now). See #4042.
member.remarks: This is every input to , which is what makes two Texts need two baked atlases - UseCustomFont included, since it decides whether Font or CustomFontFile is the identity. A property that reaches but not the cache name (the dropshadow offset and color, applied at draw time) deliberately stays out: its branches all bake the same file. Anything added to the cache name belongs here too, or only its currently-active branch gets pregenerated (#4936).

member.name: T:Gum.Bundle.GumBundleLoader
member.summary: Resolves a Gum project path to either loose-file or bundle-backed loading based on the extension of projectPath: .gumx/.gumj mean loose, .gumpkg means bundle. No sibling probing happens — the caller's chosen extension is the single source of truth, which keeps behavior identical across desktop and streaming-only platforms (Blazor WASM, Android, iOS) where a probe would otherwise issue a guaranteed-404 HTTP request. When bundle mode is selected, installs to serve bundle entries (composing with any pre-existing user hook as a fallback).

member.name: T:Gum.Bundle.GumBundleReader
member.summary:
Reads a `.gumpkg` bundle stream into a : validates header, decompresses brotli payload, and materializes every tar entry into memory.
Both the brotli decompression (BrotliSharpLib) and the tar parsing (SharpCompress) are pure-managed rather than the BCL equivalents (System.IO.Compression.BrotliStream / System.Formats.Tar). The framework versions both throw PlatformNotSupportedException on Blazor WebAssembly — brotli because Mono does not link the native brotli library, and tar because the formats package depends on POSIX file metadata APIs that aren't surfaced on browser-WASM. Blazor is the primary target the `.gumpkg` format was meant to optimize for, so the reader path must be fully managed. The on-disk format is unchanged — pure-managed and BCL implementations read the same byte stream.

member.summary: Forms properties this behavior promotes to its implementing components. member.name: P:Gum.DataTypes.Behaviors.BehaviorSave.ToolOnlyVariableReferences
member.summary: Variable reference assignments (e.g. ButtonCategoryState = IsEnabled ? "Enabled" : "Disabled") that the Gum tool evaluates at design time to drive wireframe preview from . Structural separation by name is the contract.

member.name: F:Gum.DataTypes.DimensionUnitType.Absolute
member.summary: Width and Height values are measured in absolute pixel values

member.name: F:Gum.DataTypes.DimensionUnitType.PercentageOfParent
member.summary: Width and Height values are measured in percentage of parent, where 100 is 100% of the parent's width

member.name: F:Gum.DataTypes.DimensionUnitType.RelativeToParent
member.summary: Width and Height values are measured in pixels relative to the parent, where a value of 0 equals the size of the parent. Positive values are larger than the parent. Negative values are smaller than the parent.

member.name: F:Gum.DataTypes.DimensionUnitType.PercentageOfSourceFile
member.summary: Width and Height values are measured in percentage of the source file , where 100 is 100% of the source file's width or height. Width and Height values consider texture coordinates, so if custom coordinates are used, then the Width and Height values are multplied by the visible portion of the source file.

member.name: F:Gum.DataTypes.DimensionUnitType.RelativeToChildren
member.summary: Width and Height values are measured in pixels relative to the necessary size to contain children. A larger value adds additional padding.

member.name: F:Gum.DataTypes.DimensionUnitType.PercentageOfOtherDimension
member.summary: The selected dimension is measured in percentage of the other dimension. For example, if WidthUnits is set to PercentageOfOtherDimension and Width is set to 50, then the Width is 50% of the Height. Only one of the two dimensions should use this unit type.

member.name: F:Gum.DataTypes.DimensionUnitType.MaintainFileAspectRatio
member.summary: The selected dimension is a percentage of the necessary value for maintaining the aspect ratio of the file. For example, if WidthUnits is set to MaintainFileAspectRatio and Width is set to 100, then the effective width value is set to match the aspect ratio of the file. This considers texture coordinates.

member.name: F:Gum.DataTypes.DimensionUnitType.Ratio
member.summary: The Width or Height of the parent is distributed among all siblings using Ratio after subtracting the Width and Height values of siblings using Absolute values.

member.name: F:Gum.DataTypes.DimensionUnitType.AbsoluteMultipliedByFontScale
member.summary: Width and Height values are measured in absolute pixels multiplied by the device's font scale.
member.remarks: Not all platforms support this value. If this value is not supported, absolute pixel values are used

member.name: F:Gum.DataTypes.DimensionUnitType.ScreenPixel
member.summary: Width and Height values are measured in screen pixels. If the Camera is zoomed 100% then values are the same as Absolute. Zooming the camera affects absolute size.

member.name: F:Gum.DataTypes.DimensionUnitType.RelativeToMaxParentOrChildren
member.summary: The dimension is the larger of the parent's size or the children's bounds plus padding. The value acts as pixel padding applied to the children-based calculation, similar to RelativeToChildren. A value of 0 means the element is exactly the max of its parent's size and its children's bounds.

member.name: M:Gum.DataTypes.DimensionUnitTypeExtensions.GetIsPixelBased(Gum.DataTypes.DimensionUnitType)
member.summary: Returns whether one unit represents one pixel.
member.param: The unit type.
member.returns: Whether one unit represents one pixel.

member.name: T:Gum.DataTypes.GumSyntaxVersionAttribute
member.summary: Declares the syntax version supported by a Gum runtime assembly. The Gum tool's code generator reads this attribute to determine which namespaces and conventions to use when emitting C# code for a target project.

remarks.para: When the attribute is absent from a referenced assembly, the code generator assumes pre-unification conventions. Each increment of corresponds to a set of breaking changes documented in docs/gum-tool/upgrading/syntax-versions.md.
This attribute should be applied at the assembly level in each Gum runtime project (GumCommon, MonoGameGum, RaylibGum, SkiaGum).

member.name: F:Gum.DataTypes.GumSyntaxVersionAttribute.Version
member.summary: The syntax version number. Higher values indicate newer conventions. Version 0 is the baseline (no breaking changes from the pre-attribute era). Version 1 introduced the unified Gum.GueDeriving namespace for runtime classes (non-breaking; old namespaces remain via [Obsolete] shims). Version 2 collapses ColoredCircleRuntime/ColoredRectangleRuntime/RoundedRectangleRuntime into CircleRuntime/RectangleRuntime and exposes FillColor, StrokeColor, and StrokeWidth on them. See PR #2769 / issue #2768. Version 3 unifies the GumService namespace (GumService/WindowZoomMode move under Gum, AddToRoot becomes an instance method). See PR #3122 / issue #3119. Version 4 adds RenderingLibrary.Math.Geometry.FilledStrokedRectangle, the flat fill+stroke renderable FlatRedBall's Glue codegen backs a v3 (gumx ShapeVariableExpansion) Rectangle with. See PR #4342 / issue #4341.

member.name: T:Gum.DataTypes.Serialization.Json.BoxedValueJson
member.summary: Converts a boxed (as stored by and ) to and from a set of typed, nullable JSON properties.
member.remarks: source generation cannot serialize an object-typed member polymorphically without runtime reflection, which Native AOT forbids. Rather than boxing/unboxing through a hand-written , JSON DTOs expose one nullable property per supported CLR type (mirroring the existing ValueAsString/ValueAsFloat/... XML choice pattern already used by ) and this class maps a boxed value on and off that shape. Every real project file value observed in this repo boxes one of: , , , , , or .

A boxed (e.g. DimensionUnitType.Absolute) is also accepted, converted to its underlying value. This shape only occurs on a variable that was built programmatically and never round-tripped through XML yet (e.g. StandardElementsManager's default Standards) - already stores a boxed enum on as xsi:type="xsd:int", reconstructing a plain (never the enum type) on load, so this mirrors that existing convention rather than introducing a new one.

Known, accepted limitation: 's XML shape additionally declares a [XmlElement("ValueAsObject", typeof(object))] catch-all (plus a commented-out, never-implemented ValueAsEnum case) for values outside the six supported types above. This class does not replicate that catch-all - it throws instead. Confirmed via repo-wide search: no CustomPropertySave.Value in any checked-in .gumx/.gucx/.gusx/.gutx/.behx file (including the FormsBehaviors templates) is ever populated at all, let alone with a type that would need the catch-all - every real project's CustomProperties list is empty. Revisit if a real project ever needs it.

member.name: F:Gum.DataTypes.GumProjectSave.NativeVersion
member.summary: The highest value that this version of the Gum tool supports. When a new value is added, update this constant to match.
member.remarks: The constructor still defaults to , NOT this value. That ctor default is the fallback for deserialized files that lack a Version element — a legacy file must read back as the older version so the variable-grid gate keeps hiding newer-only variables. Brand-new projects are a different case: they seed the latest variable surface up front, so the new-project factories (ProjectManager.CreateNewProject and ProjectCreator.Create) explicitly stamp this version. Marking them at the native version is honest — the project genuinely uses those features — and lets the gate show those variables immediately.

member.summary: Case-insensitive filesystems (Windows/macOS) let 's casing drift from the file actually on disk - e.g. a stale recent-projects entry recorded before the file was renamed externally. writes to verbatim, so keeping the caller-supplied casing here would silently rename the file back on the next save and break case-sensitive consumers like `gumcli pack` (#4687). member.name: M:Gum.DataTypes.GumProjectSaveExtensionMethods.MigrateCircleRadiusToWidthHeight(Gum.DataTypes.GumProjectSave)
member.summary: Issue #2947 — Circle used to expose a "Radius" variable. It now sizes via Width/Height like every other visual (the rendered radius is min(Width, Height)/2), so saved "Radius" values are converted to Width = Height = Radius * 2 to preserve existing sizes.
member.remarks: Only variables whose final name segment is exactly "Radius" are migrated, so GradientInnerRadius, GradientOuterRadius, and CornerRadius are left untouched. Handles both an unqualified "Radius" (a Circle-derived element overriding it in its own state) and a qualified "Instance.Radius" (a Circle instance inside another element).

member.name: M:Gum.DataTypes.GumProjectSaveExtensionMethods.StripCircleRectangleGradientColor1(Gum.DataTypes.GumProjectSave)
member.summary: Issue #3009 — Circle and Rectangle no longer store a standalone gradient start color (Red1/Green1/Blue1/Alpha1 / Color1); the gradient start is now the active body color (FillColor when filled, StrokeColor otherwise). Strips any orphaned Red1/Green1/Blue1/ Alpha1 variables left on Circle/Rectangle elements (and Circle/Rectangle-derived elements) and on their instances. Arc — which keeps Color1 as an obsolete back-compat shim — and the legacy RoundedRectangle/ColoredCircle shapes are left untouched.
member.remarks: Uses to resolve the root standard type, so it correctly targets only Circle/Rectangle (and derived) and skips Arc / legacy shapes. Color2 (Red2/Green2/Blue2/Alpha2 — the standalone second gradient stop) is preserved.

member.summary: While true, CustomSetPropertyOnRenderable's font-value update (bitmap font resolution/regeneration, including KernSmith dropshadow baking) is skipped entirely on every font-property assignment (both the direct-setter and string SetProperty paths). member.name: F:Gum.Wireframe.GraphicalUiElement.ResolvePopupRoots
member.summary: Resolves the popup and modal root containers used when showing a popup (for example a ComboBox or MenuItem dropdown), keyed off the element being shown. When null, callers fall back to their own default global popup/modal roots. Override this to support multiple popup/modal root pairs, for example one pair per camera/viewport in a host that embeds several independent Gum viewports. A resolved root only receives content — it is the caller's responsibility to also add it to whatever list drives input dispatch (the same mechanism used for any other root). To also opt into Gum's automatic z-order raising, canvas sizing, and modal-exclusivity handling for a resolved pair (the behavior Gum's input loop otherwise only applies to the global default popup/modal roots), register the pair in FrameworkElement.AdditionalPopupRootPairs — see that property's docs for the canvas-sizing tradeoff a per-camera root should consider before opting in.

member.name: M:Gum.Wireframe.GraphicalUiElement.UpdateLayout(Gum.Wireframe.GraphicalUiElement.ParentUpdateType,System.Int32,System.Nullable{Gum.Converters.XOrY},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Performs an update to this, and optionally to its parent and children depending on the parameters.
member.param: A filter determining whether whether to update the parent. If All is passed, then the parent will always update. If other properties are passed, then the update happens only if the parent matches the update type. For example if ParentUpdateType.IfParentStacks is passed, then an update happens if the parent stacks its children.

#3066: false for the originating call (the element whose property changed / was added), which always climbs one level so its parent re-measures; true for the propagated climbs above that, which only continue upward if their own measured size or position actually changed. This suppresses the O(N) relayout of a parent's other children when a descendant change does not alter the intermediate element's contribution to the parent.

member.name: M:Gum.Wireframe.GraphicalUiElement.GetIfShouldCallUpdateOnParent
member.summary: Returns whether a layout change on this element must notify its parent — i.e. whether the parent's own layout structurally depends on this child: the parent content-sizes (GetIfDimensionsDependOnChildren), stacks its children, or has any Ratio-sized sibling.
member.remarks: This is a purely STRUCTURAL check — it does not consider whether anything actually changed. It is called from both parent-climb sites in UpdateLayout: the unconditional originating climb and the size-gated propagated climb (#3066). The "did anything change?" gating lives at those call sites, not here, which is why the same predicate appears in two places with different surrounding conditions.

member.name: T:Gum.Wireframe.VisualOverBehavior
member.summary: Determines how to evaluate whether to show visual over states based on the HasEvents property.
member.remarks: FlatRedBall was built around the assumption that HasEvents is not enough to determine whether a visual should respond to Cursor events. This is because users may set HasEvents on a StandardElement in the Gum tool, which would default all instances of that standard to have the value set to true. This could result in controls which use this visual unexpectedly having their events swallowed by the child visual. To avoid this, FlatRedBall checks both HasEvents and whether any events are actually attached to the visual. However, this behavior is very confusing, and as new runtimes are introduced we can simplify things. To continue to support the old FRB behavior, this enum exists to allow users to select the old behavior or the new simplified behavior. Over time, we may get rid of the old behavior completely, or at least default to the new one.

member.name: T:Gum.Wireframe.GraphicalUiElementPropertyReadExtensions
member.summary: Read-side companion to : reads the current value of a Gum variable by name. A curated switch (the "base set") handles names that do not map 1:1 to a CLR property — notably the axis-aware unit enums "XUnits"/"YUnits", which the runtime stores as but the tool stores as PositionUnitType. Every other name falls through to reflection against the element's concrete runtime type, so visual properties ("Red", "Text", "Font", ...) on TextRuntime/SpriteRuntime are read without per-type code. The set of names actually requested is governed by StandardElementsManager (what Gum understands), so reflection is only ever asked for genuine Gum variables. member.name: T:Gum.GueDeriving.RenderableRegistry
member.summary: Registration point that lets optional packages — or consumers — supply renderable implementations to core -derived runtimes without core MonoGameGum referencing those packages.

remarks.para: Mirrors the existing optional-package extension pattern used by ElementSaveExtensions.RegisterGueInstantiation, StandardElementsManager.CustomGetDefaultState, and CustomSetPropertyOnRenderable.AdditionalPropertyOnRenderable: core defines the hook, an optional package (or test setup) fills it. Capabilities are keyed by type — typically a role or capability interface such as IFilledCircleRenderable.

Two registration semantics are supported, layered by priority. The general factory () is the active layer; the default factory () is the fallback. returns the active factory if one is registered, otherwise the default, otherwise null.

Each layer has both a context-free overload (Func<T>) and a context-bearing overload (Func<GraphicalUiElement, T>). The context-bearing variant lets a factory wire optional-package internal hooks onto the freshly built renderable using the caller GUE — see Apos.Shapes' OnPreRender wiring on Circle. The two buckets are independent: registering one does not clear the other, and resolution order in is active-context-bearing → active-context-free → default-context-bearing → default-context-free. Context-free only resolves context-free factories — there is no safe default to auto-pass.

Use the active layer alone (no default) for capabilities core cannot construct itself — the optional package registers a factory, callers handle null as graceful degradation. Use both layers for capabilities core ships a default implementation of that a consumer may choose to replace.

In bundle mode the enumeration is an in-memory dictionary scan; in loose mode on a real filesystem it is a single directory walk, but loose mode on a streaming platform cannot enumerate a directory over HTTP, so no animations load there — package the project as a .gumpkg to ship animations to those platforms.

member.name: M:Gum.Managers.StandardElementsManager.AddGradientVariables(Gum.DataTypes.Variables.StateSave,System.Boolean,System.Int32)
member.summary: Appends the gradient variables (UseGradient, GradientType, the gradient endpoint positions and units, the radial inner/outer radius, and the Color2 second stop) to a standard element's default state. Shared by the plain Circle/Rectangle and the legacy Skia shapes.
member.param: The default state to append the gradient variables to.

When true (the default, for Arc and the legacy ColoredCircle/RoundedRectangle/Line shapes) the standalone gradient start color channels (Red1/Green1/Blue1/Alpha1) are added. Issue #3009 — the two-slot Circle/Rectangle drive the gradient start from the active body color (FillColor/StrokeColor) instead of a standalone Color1, so they pass false and these channels are omitted entirely. Color2 (the standalone second stop) is always added.

When non-zero, stamps each appended variable's so the load-time back-fill gates them for older projects. Legacy-shape call sites pass 0 (gradients predate v3 there); the plain Circle/Rectangle pass the v3 surface version.

member.name: M:Gum.Managers.StandardElementsManager.AddDropshadowVariables(Gum.DataTypes.Variables.StateSave,System.Int32)
member.summary: Appends the dropshadow surface (HasDropshadow, offsets, blur, and color channels) to a standard element's default state. Shared by the plain Circle/Rectangle and the legacy Skia shapes (Arc/ColoredCircle/RoundedRectangle/Line).
member.param: The default state to append the dropshadow variables to.

When non-zero, stamps each appended variable's so the load-time back-fill gates them for older projects. All six current callers pass : dropshadow itself predates v3 on the legacy shapes, but #2950 renamed their per-axis DropshadowBlurX/DropshadowBlurY into this single scalar DropshadowBlur for every caller of this helper, not just Circle/Rectangle. FRB1's generated runtime for the legacy shapes (frozen outside this repo -- see SkiaGum.Renderables.RenderableArc and friends) predates that rename and never gained the scalar name, so back-filling "DropshadowBlur" into an old FRB1 project broke the regenerated runtime with CS0246. If you add a new variable to this method (or any other shared default- state helper used by these four legacy call sites), gate it explicitly -- there is no build in this repo that exercises FRB1's frozen consumer to catch a regression here.

member.name: T:Gum.Converters.RatioResizeCalculator
member.summary: Math for resizing a -typed Width/Height by a pixel-space amount. A Ratio value's rendered pixel size is availableSpace * ratioValue / sumOfRatioSiblings (siblings meaning other same-axis, same-parent instances also using Ratio), so a raw 1:1 pixel-to-ratio-number change (as used for pixel-based unit types) is wrong: it doesn't account for the siblings sharing that same pool of space.

member.name: M:Gum.Converters.RatioResizeCalculator.GetRatioDeltaForPixelDelta(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: The change to a Ratio value that reproduces of rendered pixel change, assuming the sum of all Ratio siblings' values (including this one) stays constant. Rendered pixel size is linear in the ratio value under that assumption, so scaling the ratio value by the same fraction as the desired pixel change reproduces that pixel change exactly.

member.name: M:Gum.Converters.RatioResizeCalculator.ApplyResize(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.Single},System.Single@,System.Single[]@)
member.summary: Computes new Ratio values for a dragged Ratio-typed instance and its Ratio-typed siblings (same parent, same axis) after a pixel-space resize of the dragged instance. The dragged instance's ratio changes by ; the complementary change is taken from the siblings in proportion to their current ratio values, which keeps the sum of all ratio values constant (so the total pixel space they occupy together doesn't change) and preserves the siblings' proportions relative to each other. With no siblings to redistribute to, the dragged ratio is left unchanged - changing it wouldn't produce a visible size change anyway, since a sole Ratio-typed child always fills all available space.

member.name: T:Gum.Forms.Input.Keys
member.summary: Platform-neutral keyboard key enum used by Gum Forms controls.
member.remarks:
Values and names mirror Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Input.Keys exactly — every key XNA defines, with identical numeric values and identical names. This is a permanent commitment: values will not change after ship, because user KeyCombo bindings may be serialized and changing values would silently reshuffle them.
On XNA-like runtimes (MonoGame / KNI / FNA) and FRB, KeyCombo continues to use Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Input.Keys directly and the values cast cleanly to . On non-XNA runtimes (Raylib, Sokol), KeyCombo uses and the runtime's Keyboard translates to the native key type internally.

member.name: T:Gum.Forms.Controls.IGumClipboard
member.summary: Platform-agnostic abstraction for the OS clipboard. Forms controls in GumCommon — primarily TextBox and PasswordBox — use this to read and write clipboard text on copy / cut / paste without depending on a runtime-specific clipboard library (currently TextCopy on the MonoGame side, an injected implementation on Blazor).
member.remarks: Concrete implementations are supplied by each runtime that has a clipboard story. Platforms without one (iOS today, headless test runs) leave IGumService.Clipboard null and callers no-op the copy/paste operation.

member.name: P:Gum.Forms.Controls.FrameworkElement.AdditionalPopupRootPairs
member.summary: Additional popup/modal root pairs, beyond the global /, that should receive the same automatic z-order raising, canvas sizing, and modal-exclusivity handling that FormsUtilities.Update gives the global roots. A host that resolves custom roots via (for example, one root pair per camera/viewport) should register that pair here to opt into this behavior. Registering a pair here forces its size to the full canvas every frame (matching the global roots), which is undesirable for a root that should instead track a specific camera/viewport. A host with that requirement should not register the pair here, and should instead manage its root's z-order and sizing itself while still adding its content to the list of roots passed into Update.

member.name: P:Gum.Forms.Controls.FrameworkElement.GamepadNavigationMode
member.summary: Explicitly sets (or clears, if null) how gamepad D-pad/stick input navigates focus among this element's focusable descendants — (index-based, the default) or (nearest-in-direction by on-screen position, see ). An unset element inherits the nearest ancestor's value (an explicit on a nested element opts back out of an outer zone); the root default is TabOrder. Also resolved for keyboard arrow-key navigation ( etc.) — but never for keyboard Tab/Shift+Tab, which is always index-based regardless of this setting.

member.name: P:Gum.Forms.Controls.FrameworkElement.SpatialNavigationUp
member.summary: Explicit per-direction focus overrides (Unity/UWP-style escape hatch): if set, a D-pad press in that direction — or a left-stick push snapped to its nearest cardinal — moves focus straight to the assigned element, skipping scoring entirely. Checked independently per held direction, so a diagonal press (two held) still honors whichever axis has an override set (priority order: Right, Left, Down, Up, if more than one axis has one set). Assigning a control to itself blocks that direction entirely: the press is consumed and focus stays put, rather than falling back to automatic scoring the way an unset (null) override does. Only meaningful while resolved is .

member.summary: List of key combinations that will trigger shifting focus to the previous control.

member.name: P:Gum.Forms.Controls.FrameworkElement.UpKeyCombos
member.summary: List of key combinations that request focus navigation toward whatever the resolved considers "up" — the previous element in mode, or the nearest candidate above in mode (see ). Empty by default: unlike , arrow keys are already claimed by several stock controls for their own value/selection/caret behavior (Slider, ListBox, TextBox), so wiring them up is opt-in per project rather than a default that could silently change existing behavior.

member.name: M:Gum.Forms.Controls.FrameworkElement.HandleGamepadSpatialNavigation(Gum.Input.IGamePad,Gum.Wireframe.GraphicalUiElement)
member.summary: Direction-agnostic ("spatial") focus navigation (issue #4129): reads the requested direction from the gamepad's DPad — including diagonals, from two currently-held buttons — or left analog stick, then moves focus to whichever focusable candidate under best matches that direction by on-screen position (see ), rather than by tab order. An explicit per-direction override ( etc.) on this element takes precedence over scoring, checked independently per currently-held direction (so it still applies on a diagonal press if either held axis has one set).
member.remarks: Prefer setting on a container instead of calling this directly — every stock control already calls from its own per-frame update, which resolves the mode automatically and dispatches here. If calling this directly, call it at most once per frame, for whichever single element currently has focus — do not call it from a loop over every candidate that checks per iteration, since a candidate this call just focused can still be visited later in that same loop, re-triggering navigation against the same held input and chaining multiple hops into a single press.
member.param: The gamepad to read directional input from.
The visual subtree to search for focusable candidates.

member.name: M:Gum.Forms.Controls.FrameworkElement.HandleKeyboardDirectionalNavigation
member.summary: Keyboard counterpart to (issue #4272): resolves the same and dispatches to scoring (honoring -style overrides) or index-based , driven by /// instead of a gamepad's D-pad/stick. Called once per frame from , for whichever element currently has focus.

member.name: P:Gum.Forms.Controls.ItemsControl.Items
member.summary:
The items contained by this ItemsControl. This can contain regular data such as strings, instances of ViewModels, or FrameworkElement instances such as ListBoxItem instances.
Typically the Items is assigned or bound to an ObservableCollection. In this case the ItemsControl automatically creates FrameworkElements (such as ListBoxItem instances) in response to items being added or removed from the Items list.
member.remarks:
The Items list is not guaranteed to reflect the items contained in the ItemsControl if Visual elements have been added directly to the InnerPanel. This can happen if the Visual's InnerPanel's Children are directly added to, or if an instance of an ItemsControl, such as a ListBox, is loaded from the Gum tool pre-filled with ListBoxItems.
If items are not added directly to the InnerPanel, then the Items list and the internal InnerPanel Children will remain in sync since the ItemsControl automatically creates FrameworkElement instances in response to the Items.

member.summary: Returns the Items-space index of the item visual at the given InnerPanel.Children index (skipping decorations), or -1 if the panel index is out of range or refers to a decoration. member.name: T:Gum.Forms.Controls.ListBox
member.summary: Represents a control that displays a collection of selectable items in a list, allowing users to select one item at a time. Supports keyboard, gamepad, and pointer navigation, as well as item reordering and focus management.
member.remarks: The ListBox provides advanced selection and navigation features, including support for focus management between the list as a whole and individual items, drag-and-drop reordering (when enabled), and integration with various input devices. Selection changes raise the SelectionChanged event, and controller input is handled via the ControllerButtonPushed event. The ListBox can be customized to display items using different visual templates and supports both data-bound and manually managed item collections. Thread safety is not guaranteed; all interactions should occur on the UI thread.

member.name: F:Gum.Forms.Controls.ListBox.ListBoxItemsInternal
member.summary: Provides internal storage for the collection of list box items.
member.remarks:
This field is intended for internal use and should not be accessed directly from outside the containing class. Use public members to interact with the list box items when available.
In normal usage, where view models or primitives are added to the Items collection, this list is automatically kept up-to-date. However, it is possible for the Items collection to not be up-to-date with ListBoxItemsInternal. This can happen if a visual is added directly to the Items collection. In this case, the ListBox assumes that the added visual should be directly displayed. However, if the visual already has a forms control, such as a Button having been added to the list box, then the control is used as-is, and it is not even added to the ListBoxItems.

member.name: P:Gum.Forms.Controls.ListBox.SelectedItems
member.summary: Gets the collection of currently selected items. This collection can be modified to change the selection, and supports INotifyCollectionChanged for data binding. The collection cannot be replaced, only modified.
member.remarks: In Single selection mode, this collection will contain at most one item. In Multiple and Extended modes, this collection can contain multiple items. Changes to this collection are synchronized with the IsSelected state of ListBoxItems.

member.name: P:Gum.Forms.Controls.ListBox.CanListItemsLoseFocus

member.name: P:Gum.Forms.Controls.ListBox.LoseListItemFocusOnPrimaryInput
member.summary: Whether the primary input button (usually the A button) results in the highlighted list box item being selected and in the ListBox focus moving outside of the individual items.
member.remarks: This value is true, but can be changed to false if the A button should perform actions on the highlighted list box item (such as toggling a check box) without focus being moved out of the individual items.

member.name: P:Gum.Forms.Controls.ListBox.SelectionMode
member.summary: Gets or sets the selection behavior for the ListBox.
member.remarks: Single mode (default): Only one item can be selected at a time. Multiple mode: Each click toggles selection without modifier keys. Extended mode: Click selects one, Ctrl+Click toggles, Shift+Click selects range. Note: Gamepad and keyboard input always use single-selection behavior regardless of this mode.

member.name: P:Gum.Forms.Controls.TextBoxBase.ShowNativeKeyboardOnFocus
member.summary:
If true, focusing this control displays the OS-provided modal keyboard dialog (via MonoGame's Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Input.KeyboardInput.Show). The text entered in the dialog is applied to this control when the user accepts. Defaults to true on Android and iOS, and false on every other platform, because:
Desktop (Windows/Mac/Linux): hardware keyboard input works directly, and the native dialog is a stub — enabling it would break normal typing.
Web (Blazor WebAssembly, including mobile browsers): KeyboardInput.Show is not implemented on the browser runtime, so the call is bypassed regardless of this flag. Note that a mobile device running the game inside a browser reports IsBrowser(), not IsAndroid()/IsIOS().
You can override the default by setting this property explicitly after the control is created.

member.name: P:Gum.Forms.Controls.TextBoxBase.TextWrapping
member.summary: Controls visual wrapping behavior of the displayed text. When set to , text that exceeds the container's width wraps to additional visual lines. When (the default), text continues horizontally and the visible region scrolls horizontally to keep the caret in view.
member.remarks:
This property is independent of :
NoWrap, AcceptsReturn=false (default) — single-line input. The text never grows vertically through user typing; horizontal scrolling keeps the caret visible.
NoWrap, AcceptsReturn=true — code-editor feel. User can type Enter for explicit newlines; long lines overflow horizontally rather than wrapping.
Wrap, AcceptsReturn=false — read-mostly multi-line display. Long text wraps; user can't add explicit newlines via Enter.
Wrap, AcceptsReturn=true — standard multi-line text area.
The Visual is placed in its "Multi" / "MultiNoWrap" LineModeCategory state whenever either property would produce vertical content (wrapping enabled OR Enter inserts newlines); otherwise the "Single" state is used. Vertical scrolling is enabled in any non-single state; horizontal scrolling is enabled whenever wrapping is off.

member.summary: Brings up the platform's native text-input UI on behalf of this control, if one is available. Keyboards reporting (Android) show the inline soft keyboard; everywhere else the call is delegated to the registered on IGumService.Default.NativeTextInput — runtimes without a native dialog leave that property null and the call no-ops. Internal so tests can drive the focus-show flow directly.

member.name: P:Gum.Forms.Controls.TextBoxBase.AcceptsReturn
member.summary: Controls whether pressing the Enter / Return key inserts a newline ('\n') into the text. When false (the default), Enter is treated as a commit gesture (binding sources with UpdateSourceTrigger.LostFocus are pushed) and no newline is added.
member.remarks:
This property only governs the keyboard behavior. It does NOT control visual layout directly, and it does NOT prevent the underlying text from containing '\n' characters — code that assigns programmatically, paste, and so on can introduce newlines regardless of this setting.
The Visual's "Multi" / "MultiNoWrap" LineModeCategory state is selected when either is true or is ; setting this property alone to true with wrapping off produces the "MultiNoWrap" state (top-aligned, lines may overflow horizontally). See for the full mode matrix.

member.name: P:Gum.Forms.Controls.TextBoxBase.IsSingleLineMode
member.summary:
True when the text box is configured as single-line — neither is set to nor is enabled. This is the inverse of the condition that drives the Visual into its "Multi" / "MultiNoWrap" state.
"Single-line" here refers to configuration intent, not the actual content: the underlying text can still contain '\n' characters (assigned programmatically or via paste) and render across multiple visual lines, but the layout uses the "Single" state and vertical scrolling is disabled. This intentional asymmetry matches the invariant that single-line text boxes never shift the text vertically, even in pathological cases.

member.name: P:Gum.Forms.Controls.TextBoxBase.IsRenderedAsSingleLine
member.summary:
True when the displayed text actually occupies one visual line, so caret, selection and hit-test positions can be measured against the whole string instead of per wrapped line.
Unlike this reflects layout rather than configuration. A single-line-configured box still renders multiple lines when the assigned text contains '\n', or when the visual's text instance is sized relative to its parent and wraps. Measuring those as one line puts the caret hundreds of pixels right of the glyph it belongs to, and the horizontal scroll then drags the text left to chase it (issue #4393).

member.name: P:Gum.Forms.Controls.TextBoxBase.DoesTextComponentWrap
member.summary: True when the text component is sized against its parent, which makes it wrap. Every visual line then fits the container by construction, so horizontal scrolling would only push characters out of the clipped region — most visibly on the keystroke that wraps a line, where the caret sits past the right edge by the width of the trailing space.

member.name: M:Gum.Forms.Controls.TextBoxBase.UpdateStateForSingleOrMultiLine
member.summary:
Applies the appropriate LineModeCategory state on the Visual based on the current and values:
"Single" — neither wrapping nor Enter-to-newline; the visual is laid out for a single line.
"Multi" — wrapping is enabled (with or without AcceptsReturn).
"MultiNoWrap" — AcceptsReturn is enabled but wrapping is not. Falls back to "Multi" if the visual doesn't define a separate state for this case.
Called whenever either property changes.

member.name: T:Gum.Forms.SpatialNavigationService
member.summary: Scores focusable candidates by on-screen distance and angular alignment to a requested direction, and picks the best match — the geometric core of direction-agnostic ("spatial") focus navigation (issue #4129). Stateless and read-only: it only reads already-resolved absolute (screen-space) bounds off the visual tree and does not mutate focus itself; callers (see 's gamepad navigation methods) apply the result.

member.name: M:Gum.Forms.SpatialNavigationService.FindBestCandidate(Gum.Forms.Controls.FrameworkElement,System.Single,System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{Gum.Forms.Controls.FrameworkElement},System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Returns whichever element best matches from , or null if none qualify. Distance and angle are measured between the closest points of the origin's and each candidate's rectangles (the AABB gap along each axis, zero on an axis where the two rectangles' ranges overlap), not raw center-to-center — either rectangle can be wide (e.g. a full-width Slider as the origin or as a candidate) and have its center sit far enough to the side that a center-based angle falls outside the direction cone, even though the rectangles are directly across from each other. Candidates outside the direction cone ( either side of the requested angle) are excluded so navigation never moves backwards; among the rest, the lowest distance * (1 + angleWeight * angleDiff / maxAngleRadians) score wins.
member.param: The currently-focused element navigation is relative to.
The requested direction in screen space: 0 = right, increasing clockwise (Y grows downward).

The focusable elements to consider. , any ancestor of (e.g. a large focusable container the origin sits near the edge of), and any candidate nested inside or inside another candidate (e.g. a composite control's own internal focusable part, such as a Slider's Thumb button) are skipped if present — an ancestor's own center can otherwise score better than a true sibling simply by virtue of containing the origin, and an internal part sitting right at its owning control's edge can otherwise outscore that control (or an unrelated sibling) simply by virtue of being nested inside it. This mirrors index-based , which treats a focusable element as an opaque stop and never descends into it.
Half-width of the direction cone; candidates outside are excluded.
How strongly angular misalignment penalizes an otherwise-close candidate.

member.summary: How a frame's per-frame color (/ /) combines with the sprite's texture, matching FlatRedBall2's ColorOperation enum (FlatRedBall2.Animation.ColorOperation) authored by the FlatRedBall Animation Editor.

member.name: F:Gum.Content.AnimationChain.AnimationFrameColorOperation.Add
member.summary: Add the color to the texture (brighten / glow / flash). Black (0) is the identity. Applied on MonoGame/KNI/FNA (#4792 Gap 2) as a second additive draw pass rather than a custom shader: the normal draw, then the same sprite drawn again with the additive color blended on top and destination alpha preserved. Because clamping happens after the additive blend instead of in one pass, semi-transparent edges over a mid-tone background can come out a bit hotter than a true single-pass Add would — acceptable for silhouettes and flashes. raylib, Skia, and NineSlice's equivalent frame-apply path don't implement this yet and silently drop it (tracked as a follow-up to #4792).

member.name: T:RenderingLibrary.Content.IContentLoader
member.summary: Strategy for turning a content name (typically a file path) into a loaded asset such as a texture or font. Each rendering backend (MonoGame/KNI/FNA, Raylib, Skia, and so on) ships its own implementation.
member.remarks:
The active loader is held by ; assign your own implementation there to customize how Gum resolves assets — for example, to load from a custom asset store, or to hand back an asset your game engine has already loaded so the same texture is not loaded into memory twice. A custom loader typically wraps (delegates to) the built-in loader for any content name it does not handle, so default loading and caching are preserved.
Implementations are responsible for their own caching. See the remarks on for why caching lives in the loader rather than in .

member.name: T:RenderingLibrary.Graphics.LayerCameraSettings
member.summary: Per-layer camera overrides that let a ignore, replace, or offset the main 's position and zoom.
member.remarks: Assigning a to a changes how both rendering and cursor hit-testing are performed for objects on that layer. When this value is (the default), the layer uses the main camera unchanged.

member.name: P:RenderingLibrary.Graphics.LayerCameraSettings.IsInScreenSpace
member.summary: Whether the layer is rendered in screen space, ignoring the main camera's position.
member.remarks:
When , objects on this layer are positioned relative to the screen rather than the world: moving the main has no effect on where they appear. This is typically used for HUDs, overlays, and other UI that should stay fixed on the screen while a world camera scrolls.
and still apply when this is ; they are simply applied on top of the screen origin instead of the main camera's world position.

member.name: P:RenderingLibrary.Graphics.LayerCameraSettings.Zoom
member.summary: Overrides the main camera's zoom for this layer. If , the main camera's zoom is used.
member.remarks: A value of 1 means no zoom, 2 means rendered objects appear twice as large, and 0.5 means half size. This is applied independently of the main camera's zoom, so a UI layer can remain at 1:1 while a world layer zooms.

member.name: F:RenderingLibrary.Graphics.LayerCameraSettings.Position
member.summary: An additional camera position applied to this layer, or to use the main camera's position unchanged.
member.remarks:
This value represents a camera position, not a layer offset. Because moving a camera in one direction makes the world appear to move in the opposite direction, the sign convention is the reverse of what you might expect if you are thinking of it as "shift the layer by this amount":
A positive moves the camera right, which makes the layer's content appear to shift left on screen.
A positive moves the camera down (Gum uses a Y-down screen convention for the main camera), which makes the layer's content appear to shift up on screen. A negative Y makes the content shift down.
When is , this value is added to the main camera's position for this layer. When is , the main camera's position is ignored and this value is used on its own.
Rendering and cursor hit-testing both respect this value, so a cursor's world position on this layer is consistent with where its objects draw.

member.name: P:RenderingLibrary.Graphics.Layer.LayerCameraSettings

This is the inverse of and is used by GumService.Draw(Matrix) so that callers can drive Gum's camera from a platform-native transform (raylib's Camera2D via GetCameraMatrix2D, MonoGame's view matrix, etc.). The margin absorbs content that bleeds slightly past its own bounds (drop shadows, borders) so it is not prematurely culled.

member.name: M:RenderingLibrary.CameraScissorExtensions.GetCullTestBoundsFor(RenderingLibrary.Camera,RenderingLibrary.Graphics.Layer,RenderingLibrary.Graphics.IRenderableIpso)
member.summary:
Like , but for renderables whose actual drawn extent can exceed their own declared bounds, expands the world-space Top/Bottom before transforming so the off-screen cull doesn't skip content that is still genuinely on screen. The only known case today is wrapped/multi-line text whose Height is an independent layout constraint rather than derived from its content — e.g. a multi-line Forms TextBox, which scrolls by moving Y while Height stays fixed to the visible box. Its (the actual rendered extent) can then be far larger than Height, so the object's own declared bounds drift entirely outside the clip as it scrolls, even though the currently-visible lines should still draw (#4144).
The expansion is symmetric (both Top and Bottom, by the same excess) because this method doesn't know the text's vertical alignment (top/center/bottom) — a symmetric expansion is the smallest adjustment guaranteed to cover the true rendered span under any of the three.
Used only for the off-screen cull decision (#2998) — is still used, unmodified, to apply the actual GPU clip for ClipsChildren renderables, so this never changes what's visually cropped, only what gets culled.

member.name: T:RenderingLibrary.WheelZoomAccumulator
member.summary: Turns a stream of mouse-wheel delta reports into discrete zoom-level steps, at the same one-step-per-notch cadence a physical mouse wheel produces. A real wheel reports one notch ( units) per event; a trackpad's two-finger scroll/pinch instead reports many events per second, each with a small delta, so consuming delta magnitude directly (rather than just its sign) is what keeps a trackpad gesture from racing through many zoom levels a mouse wheel would only reach after many physical clicks.

member.name: F:RenderingLibrary.WheelZoomAccumulator.NotchDelta
member.summary: Wheel delta representing one physical mouse-wheel notch (WPF/Avalonia convention).

member.name: M:RenderingLibrary.WheelZoomAccumulator.Consume(System.Int32)
member.summary: Feeds one wheel-delta report in. Returns 1 or -1 once the running total crosses a full notch in that direction (consuming exactly one notch's worth from the total and carrying any remainder to the next call), or 0 if no notch has been reached yet. A delta against the carried total's direction drops the total first, so a reversal never steps the old way.

member.name: M:GumRuntime.ElementSaveExtensions.GetItemNamesOwnedByReachableCategorizedStates(Gum.DataTypes.Variables.StateSave,Gum.DataTypes.InstanceSave)
member.summary: Returns the set of qualified item names (e.g. "TextInstance.FontSize" or "TextInstance.VariableReferences") owned by reachable categorized states on in . "Owned" covers three shapes: (a) Local VariableReferences rows on this state that target the instance (their LHSes are scalar names owned by those refs). (b) VariableReferences rows on the matched categorized state of the instance's BaseType — both the LHSes (scalar names) AND a marker for the list itself ("<instance>.VariableReferences") so paste can drop a base-snapshotted ref row that would shadow the categorized walk. (c) Direct scalar variables on that matched categorized state — their names are owned even without a reference, because the state's direct set would otherwise be shadowed by a base-level scalar of the same name. The instance type's BaseType chain is walked via GetStateSaveRecursively. Used by copy/paste to filter base-element captures so the new instance picks up the active categorized state instead of inheriting the source's base-level orphans/overrides.

member.name: M:GumRuntime.ElementSaveExtensions.ExpandCompositeReferenceLine(System.String,Gum.DataTypes.ElementSave)
member.summary: Expands a single reference line into one line per channel when its left side is a composite property whose right side ends in another composite name of the *same* underlying token (e.g. Color = Other.Color, or a cross-named DropshadowColor = Other.FillColor). Left and right channel names are paired positionally (channel order is fixed per descriptor - e.g. Red/Green/Blue), so the two sides don't need identical composite names, only the same composite token (both "Color", not one "Color" and one "CornerRadius"). Returns the line unchanged (as a single-item sequence) when it isn't a composite reference. This is what lets the collapsed form stay on disk while every apply/evaluate/validate path downstream only ever sees plain single-channel lines. Public so other GumCommon-tier consumers of raw VariableReferences line text (e.g. HeadlessErrorChecker's reference-conflict check) can expand consistently with how references are actually applied, instead of duplicating the channel table.
